tldr:
For a confounding-adjusted causal risk difference, this paper proves a complete finite-sample frontier in a structured symmetric randomized-response benchmark with public uniform scalar design and independent deterministic true-one calibration probes. With \(N=nd^2\) and \(M=md^2\), minimax absolute risk and finite honest connected interval length both have order
\[
1\wedge\max\{N^{-1/2},M^{-2/7},(nN)^{-1/7},(NM)^{-1/7}\}.
\]
Explicit data-only cubic estimators and intervals attain this rate, and matching original-record Bernoulli converses hold over the identical \(\mathcal M\), without an essential logarithm. The proved mixed branch \((nmd^4)^{-1/7}\) is active precisely when \(N,M\ge1\) and \(N\le M\le\min(n,N^{5/2})\), with boundary ties. On \(d=n^{-1/4}\), \(m=\lceil n^{5/4}\rceil\), the joint order exceeds both the entire-curve oracle and pure-calibration numerical benchmark orders by \(n^{1/28}\). This obstruction determines calibration budgets needed to preserve known-channel precision. Identification and validation-aware efficient estimation remain credited to prior work. The theorem is a prospective benchmark for the outcome-misclassification risk-difference question, rather than a converse for Wei et al.'s different combined-sample validation experiment.
gap: Wei et al. supplies identification and validation-aware estimation. Ordinary-density cubic and two-sample functional results supply methods but do not state a frontier uniform in a weakening unknown channel with rough propensity and independent effect-free probes.
fill: The joint frontier question requires an evaluated attainable rate and identical-class all-procedure converse at every finite budget, then derives consistency and oracle-retaining calibration orders. The decisive proof obligations are source-slot covariance, nested-bin cancellation, and cross-source mixture affinity.
